title: Nana's Got an Anchor
subject: A grandmother who has never been to sea gets an anchor tattooed on her forearm for her seventieth birthday and hides it under cardigans all summer from her disapproving daughter, who finally rolls up her own sleeve to show a swallow hidden since 1996.
caption: Sea shanty, traditional British call-and-response work shanty with a rowdy pub-session feel. Crew chorus with foot stomps and hand claps on the beat, anglo concertina pumping chords, fiddle doubling the tune with droning double-stops, bodhran hand drum on a steady thump. Live pub-room recording, stomps and claps close to the mics. Male baritone shantyman, strong open chest voice, every line answered by a mixed crew chorus in unison. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 100 BPM, D minor. Rowdy, fond, cheeky. No drum kit, no electric guitar, no synths, no autotune, no rap, no pop production.
lyrics:
[Intro - concertina, stomps, bodhran]

[Verse 1]
Nana turned seventy in the month of May
Never been to sea, not a single day
Walked in a tattoo parlour on the quay
Said, an anchor on my forearm, lad, for me

[Pre-Chorus]
Heave away, heave away
Never been to sea, heave away

[Chorus]
Oh, Nana's got an anchor, heave away, haul away
Hid beneath her cardigan all through the day
Nana's got an anchor and she's not going to say
Heave away, my Nana, heave away

[Verse 2]
Her daughter says, Mother, it's thirty degrees
Why the cardigan, why the sleeves
Then the daughter rolls her own sleeve high
There's a swallow from ninety-six, oh my

[Pre-Chorus]
Heave away, heave away
Who's the sailor now, I say

[Chorus]
Oh, Nana's got an anchor, and the daughter's got a bird
Hid beneath the cardigans, and neither said a word
Two of them have inked their arms, and both are rather proud
Heave away, my Nana, sing it loud

[Outro - concertina, fiddle, stomps]
Heave away, my Nana, heave away
